titulo: Entity: telling search engines who is behind the site
lead: Content only you can write starts by saying who "you" are. Google and AI tools gather pages, profiles, and mentions into an entity: a person, a brand. If the site doesn't declare this in one single way, each page looks like it was written by a different author, and your name can even be confused with someone else's.
objetivo: declare a Person and an Organization with a fixed @id and a separate sameAs, and make the rest of the site point to them.

aprende.t: What an entity is and why it comes before content
The JSON-LD template with author and brand under a fixed @id
How article, news, and course point to the same entity
Testing whether AI tools confuse your name with another

hero_alt: A hand hands over a badge at the front desk of a small office, with business cards neatly arranged on the counter.

secoes.titulo: One entity, many pages pointing to it

nos.detalhe: A single person, with an identity address that never changes, like https://www.seusite.com/#autor. It isn't a page: it's a stable label that the other markup refers to.
The organization, with its own @id (#organizacao). Author and brand are linked: the author works for the brand, and the brand has the author as its founder.
No page repeats the name, logo, and profiles by hand. Each one points to the @id, and the search engine understands it's always the same person and the same brand.

A list of profiles that prove the identity. The person's profiles go in the Person; the brand's profiles go in the Organization. Mixing them makes the search engine think the person and the brand are the same thing.
Subdomains and sister sites use the same @id: to Google, it's a single entity. The markup must match what is written on the page; it confirms, it doesn't invent.

secoes.legenda: Declare once, point always: the rest of the course writes content on behalf of this entity.

secoes.titulo: Build the entity in four steps

texto: Use the canonical domain from course 1 and a fragment: #autor and #organizacao. Don't change them again.
If you have subdomains (news, events), they all use exactly the same @id values as the main site.
Name, "about" page, logo, and the official profiles. Only profiles that exist and that you control.
The "about" page must say, in visible text, the same thing the markup says.
The entity block goes into the layout, the same on every page.
The markup on each page (article, news, course) points to it by @id, without repeating data.

exemplo.texto: On 09/24/2026, Person #nei and Organization #organization started appearing on every page of the portal (commit 965d901).

texto: Ask two assistants "what is [your brand]?" If the answer talks about another company or agency, you have a name collision.
Markup alone doesn't solve a collision: it takes pages that clearly say who you are, and consistent profiles.

secoes.titulo: The entity template and a page pointing to it
secoes.sub: Swap in your domain, names, and profiles. Don't invent a profile that doesn't exist.

blocos.rot: Check it in the course 1 X-ray
blocos.conteudo:
tools/auditoria.sh https://www.seusite.com / /sobre/ /um-artigo/
# look for the JSON-LD line of each page: Person and Organization on all of them

Entity test on <dd/mm/yyyy>
Question: "what is <your brand>?"
- Assistant 1: <talks about me | talks about someone else: who? | doesn't know>
- Assistant 2: <talks about me | talks about someone else: who? | doesn't know>
Collision? <yes/no>. What I will write on the page about: <...>

abas.html:
JSON-LD from the inema.club home page, only the items with @id:

EducationalOrganization  https://www.inema.club/#organization  sameAs: 5
Person                   https://www.inema.club/#nei           sameAs: 1
WebSite                  https://www.inema.club/#website

On a question page of the same site:

publisher → {"@id": "https://www.inema.club/#organization"}

On 07/10/2026, INEMA's fixed battery of 20 questions ran on Claude and Gemini. INEMA showed up in 0 of 48 neutral answers on Claude and in 0 of 4 on Gemini.

Worse: "What is INEMA?" got 4 of 4 answers about INEMA-BA, an environmental agency. After that, 54 listing pages were published under /conhecimento/ saying who INEMA is.

• One @id per page: it becomes a new entity on every page.
  • Mixed-up sameAs: the person's profile on the brand, and vice versa.
  • Markup the text doesn't confirm: Google asks that the structure match what's visible.

secoes.sub: Use the canonical domain you chose in course 1.

exercicios.texto: Fill in the template with your data, put it in the site layout, and make at least one page type (article, product, or course) point to the @id. Publish and run the X-ray on 3 pages.
exercicios.pronto: the schema.org validator shows Person and Organization with no errors, and the X-ray shows both on all 3 pages.

exercicios.texto: Ask "what is [your brand]?" and "who is [your name]?" on two assistants. Fill in the notes.
exercicios.pronto: the notes say, for each assistant, whether it talked about you, about someone else (who), or didn't know, and what you will write on the "about" page.

secoes.sub: The explanation shows up after your answer.

perguntas.p: The news site is a subdomain of the main site. Which @id does it use for the organization?
opcoes: The same @id as the main site.
None: news doesn't need an entity.
perguntas.explica: The same @id on every site and subdomain: to Google, it's a single entity. One @id per site splits the identity.

perguntas.p: Where do the personal LinkedIn and the brand's Instagram profiles go?
opcoes: LinkedIn on the Person, Instagram on the Organization.
Only in the footer, with no markup.
perguntas.explica: Separate sameAs: the person's profiles on the Person, the brand's profiles on the Organization. Mixing them confuses person and brand.

perguntas.p: "What is [your brand]?" comes back talking about a public agency with the same name. What is this?
opcoes: Name collision: the assistant knows another entity with your name.
perguntas.explica: That was the case with INEMA and INEMA-BA. The way out is to make clear who you are, with consistent pages and profiles, and measure again later.

perguntas.p: The markup says the author is an expert with 20 years of experience, but the page doesn't mention it. Is that okay?
opcoes: It's fine, markup is for robots.
No: the structure has to match the visible text.
It's fine if it's in the sameAs.
It's fine, but only for AI.
perguntas.explica: Google asks that structured data confirm what the page shows. Markup with no text to back it up is a fabricated signal.

itens.texto: One author and one brand, the same on every page and subdomain.
Article, news, and course cite the @id.
A name collision shows up when you ask the question and write down the answer.
There is no special schema for AI: an entity matters because it says who is behind the content and matches the text.
